bull.t: Expansion of in vivo CAR-T platform
bull.b: The Senlang agreement expands Tempest’s potential in vivo CAR-T platform into hematologic malignancies and autoimmune diseases, while the partner’s Phase 1 candidate provides clinical-stage validation. If exercised, the option could broaden the pipeline and strengthen strategic positioning.

A committed equity facility gives Tempest discretion to access capital over time rather than raising the full amount at once. That flexibility can support clinical development and corporate needs, although future share issuance may dilute existing holders.

Adding an experienced finance and capital-markets director can improve oversight as Tempest advances its CAR-T pipeline and manages funding needs. His background may support more disciplined capital allocation, financing execution and strategic development over multiple quarters.

bear.b: Tempest has no current revenue base to offset research and development spending, while losses remain substantial and recurring. Without commercialization or partnering progress, the company lacks operating leverage and must continue relying on external funding to advance its programs.

Ongoing cash outflows combined with negative stockholders’ equity reduce financial flexibility and increase dependence on additional financing. This weak capital structure may constrain development choices and heighten refinancing or dilution risk if funding conditions become less favorable.

bear.t: Repeated failure to approve governance reforms
bear.b: Repeated adjournments show that Tempest has been unable to secure the supermajority approval needed for proposed governance changes. This can delay greater shareholder voting flexibility, prolong governance friction and complicate the company’s ability to execute structural corporate actions.
